strategy.thesis: Hospital-backed 'VC × accelerator × hospital' model: Taiwan's largest medtech/healthtech accelerator partners directly with hospitals to give precision-medicine, medical-device and digital-health startups real clinical validation sites, cutting commercialization timelines from 7-8 years to 3-5 years and serving as a gateway into Asia.

investment.raw: PoC program guarantees US$500,000 investment in one selected startup

perks: Clinical validation sites at partner hospitals
20-30 physician consultants per hospital per year
Access to Taipei Medical University, Show Chwan (秀傳), Kaohsiung Medical University networks
program.eligibility: Precision-medicine, medical-device and digital-health startups (PoC clinical-validation track runs 5-6 months)

application.how_to_apply: Apply to the PoC clinical-validation accelerator open calls via behealthventures.com

summary.en: BE Health Ventures (比翼生醫, formerly BE Accelerator / BE Capital) is Taiwan's largest medtech and healthtech startup accelerator and a hospital-backed VC, founded around 2018. Using a 'VC × accelerator × hospital' model with partners including Taipei Medical University, Show Chwan and Kaohsiung Medical University, it has mentored 140+ biomedical startups and invested in roughly 30; its 25 invested portfolio companies have raised about US$200M in total. Its PoC clinical-validation program (5-6 months) guarantees a US$500K investment in one selected startup, and it is expanding into Japan.
summary.local: 比翼生醫(前身 BE Accelerator / BE Capital)是台灣最大的醫療科技/生技新創加速器,也是「醫院創投」,約 2018 年成立。以「創投 × 加速器 × 醫院」整合模式,與臺北醫學大學、秀傳醫療體系、高雄醫學大學等合作,已輔導 140+ 海內外生醫新創、直接投資近 30 家;25 間投資項目公司募資總額約 2 億美元。其 PoC 臨床實證計畫(5-6 個月)保證投資其中一家新創 50 萬美元,並正布局日本市場。

strategy.thesis: Taiwan's first fintech-focused hub and accelerator, set up under the guidance of the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and planned by the Taiwan Financial Services Roundtable (TFSR), executed by the Institute for Information Industry (III). It bundles the whole local fintech ecosystem under one roof with a Digital Sandbox, Regulation Clinic and Global Connection to grow startups in payments, wealthtech, insurtech, regtech, blockchain, eKYC/eAML and AI.

summary.en: FinTechSpace (金融科技創新園區) is Taiwan's first fintech-focused co-working hub and accelerator, opened in September 2018 under the guidance of the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), planned by the Taiwan Financial Services Roundtable (TFSR) and executed by the Institute for Information Industry (III) — building on the earlier FintechBase. Its first residency wave admitted 37 teams from 64 applicants (31 domestic, 6 international), and it has supported 200+ fintech startups across payments, wealthtech, insurtech, regtech, blockchain, eKYC/eAML and AI, supported by a Digital Sandbox, Regulation Clinic and 100+ partner organizations.

strategy.thesis: Taiwan's first and largest agri-food tech accelerator, run by the non-profit HAOSHi Foundation (funded by the Ting Hsin Wei-Te Charity Fund). It runs a free ~4-month program across two pillars — Agri-Food Supply Chain Tech and Food Innovation & Commercialization — covering food biotech, precision nutrition, alternative protein, packaging, logistics, FMCG and circular sustainability.

investment.raw: free 4-month program (no equity); refundable NT$20,000 admission deposit

application_cycles: Annual; rolling admissions through 31 March, kickoff in May, Demo Day in October

summary.en: HAOSHi Accelerator (好食好事) is Taiwan's first and largest agri-food tech accelerator, founded in 2018 by the non-profit HAOSHi Foundation (established 2017 by the Ting Hsin Wei-Te Charity Fund). Its free ~4-month program (no equity; refundable NT$20,000 deposit) covers agri-food supply-chain tech, food biotech, alternative protein and precision nutrition. Since 2018 it has accelerated 78+ startups with 60-70+ mentors; alumni report cumulative revenue of US$1.8B+ and follow-on investment of US$108.8M+, with a 40%+ investment rate.

summary.en: Foodland Ventures (扶田資本) is described as Taiwan's first foodtech/agrifood-tech focused VC and accelerator, founded by serial foodtech entrepreneur Victor Chen (also behind Food Innovation Summit Taiwan and NOM Magazine). summary.en: Wistron Accelerator (緯創加速器) is a corporate vertical accelerator launched in 2021 by Taiwanese hardware giant Wistron, operated by AppWorks. It runs twice a year, recruits about 7 startups per batch in AI, IoT, cloud and cybersecurity (also edutech/medtech), and is equity-free and fee-free, instead giving NT$200,000 sponsorship and direct access to Wistron Group C-level mentors. Across its first eight batches it selected 40 startups and made 36 investments.

summary.en: StarFab Accelerator (founded 2016) is a Taipei-based corporate accelerator focused on Industry 4.0 / deep tech, matching IoT, hardware-software, cloud, big data and AI-robotics startups with major Taiwanese corporations (Delta, Advantech, Chunghwa Telecom, Far EasTone, Inventec) via a reverse-pitch model across six specializations. strategy.thesis: Taipei-based, mobile-first/mobile-only accelerator by US VC SOSV targeting the 'next 4 billion' mobile-only users in emerging markets (India, Indonesia, the rest of SEA and South Asia). Instead of selling equity to buy ads, startups get free user-acquisition support and capital in return for revenue share and equity, focusing on positive unit economics first.

perks: Free user-acquisition / cross-promotion across MOX ecosystem
program.eligibility: Consumer-facing mobile app/service startups targeting emerging markets

application.how_to_apply: Historically applied via SOSV / MOX cohort calls (program wound down)

summary.en: MOX (Mobile Only Accelerator) was a Taipei-based, mobile-first/mobile-only accelerator run by US VC firm SOSV — the first international accelerator in Taiwan — targeting the 'next 4 billion' mobile-only consumers in India, Indonesia and the rest of Southeast Asia. SOSV invested US$100K-120K per company in cohorts of ~10 startups (8-week program) in return for revenue share and equity, ran 10+ cohorts/Demo Days, and backed companies like ELSA and Achiko (which listed on Switzerland's SIX Exchange). The program has since wound down.

verification_notes: Operated from Taipei (so within the Taiwan bucket) but invests in emerging-market consumer-mobile startups globally; run by US firm SOSV. Founded ~2016 (first batch). Investment US$100K-120K per company; equity % not fixed (revenue-share + equity). Marked 'inactive' as SOSV wound down its accelerator-as-VC programs (MOX/Chinaccelerator) in the early 2020s; 10+ cohorts ran. Included as a sector-specific (mobile/consumer) accelerator distinct from generalist Taiwan accelerators.

name.local: SPARK Taiwan 生醫轉譯計畫

strategy.thesis: Government-backed biomedical translational accelerator adapting Stanford's SPARK model to Taiwan: an education-, mentorship- and commercialization-focused program that helps academic researchers advance new drugs, devices and technologies from the lab toward startups and technology transfer.

investment.raw: translational project funding / mentorship (government program, no equity)

program.eligibility: Academic / university biomedical research teams pursuing translation and commercialization

track_record.portfolio_count: 400+ projects (2013-2023); 65 startups formed; 55 technology transfers; 2,000+ trainees

application.how_to_apply: Apply as an academic biomedical research team via the SPARK Taiwan / Si2C program

summary.en: SPARK Taiwan is a government-backed biomedical translational accelerator established in 2013 by the Taiwan Supra Integration and Incubation Center (Si2C) under the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC), adapting Stanford's SPARK model. It mentors academic researchers in advancing drugs, devices and technologies toward commercialization. From 2013-2023 it supported 400+ projects, resulting in 65 startups and 55 technology transfers, and trained 2,000+ graduate students, postdocs and early-career scientists.
summary.local: SPARK Taiwan 是 2013 年由 Taiwan Supra Integration and Incubation Center(Si2C)在國家科學及技術委員會(NSTC)下成立的生醫轉譯加速計畫,移植史丹佛 SPARK 模式,輔導學界研究者將新藥、醫材與技術推向商品化。2013-2023 年間支持 400+ 項目,催生 65 家新創與 55 件技轉,並培訓 2,000+ 研究生、博士後與早期研究人才。

verification_notes: SPARK Taiwan is a university-based translational-medicine accelerator/training program rather than a cash-for-equity cohort accelerator; included as a biotech sector accelerator/incubator. Metrics (400+ projects, 65 startups, 55 tech transfers, 2,000+ trainees over 2013-2023) come from SPARK Stanford and Asia Research News (echoing a Nature Biotechnology paper). No equity taken; program length/cohort size not standardized. Administered via Si2C under NSTC, with multiple participating universities/medical centers.

aka: Impact Hub Taipei 影響力孵化器

strategy.thesis: Local node of the global Impact Hub network and an impact-focused incubator/accelerator for social innovation and SDG-aligned ventures. Its 2030 Impact Accelerator (2030IA) — its first global impact accelerator — offers capacity-building, expert mentoring and connections to international impact investors to scale social enterprises toward the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals.

perks: Connections to international impact investors and organizations
program.eligibility: Social enterprises / impact-driven and SDG-aligned startups

application.how_to_apply: Apply to the 2030 Impact Accelerator or incubation programs via taipei.impacthub.net

summary.en: Impact Hub Taipei is the Taipei node of the global Impact Hub network and an impact-focused incubator/accelerator for social innovation. It has incubated 50+ teams, and its 2030 Impact Accelerator (2030IA) — its first global impact accelerator — provides capacity-building, expert mentoring and connections to international impact investors for SDG-aligned social enterprises such as Sense Innovation (assistive eye-movement software) and Donkey Move (inclusive elderly transport).
summary.local: Impact Hub Taipei 是全球 Impact Hub 網絡的台北據點,也是聚焦社會創新的影響力孵化器/加速器,已孵化 50+ 團隊。其「2030 Impact Accelerator(2030IA)」是首個全球影響力加速器,為對齊 SDGs 的社會企業(如 Sense Innovation 輔助眼動軟體、Donkey Move 共融長者運輸)提供能力建構、專家輔導與國際影響力投資人連結。
